summary: Hosted tariff applied to traffic despite reserved model pin during planned eu-west maintenance
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that a subset of production requests on 2026-03-09 02:10-02:40 UTC were billed at hosted (pay-as-you-go) tariff despite having pinned their tenancy to a reserved model on Dedicated capacity. Impact: Unexpected charges on their invoice and an auto-invoice failure due to a temporary overage that pushed them above their reserved threshold. Environment: eu-west production (dedicated cluster id: ded-eu-021).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer uses API key xxxxx-REDACTED from org brightnote-prod with pinning header 'X-Model-Pin: redwood/open-7b-v2-pin-2026-02-15'
2) At 2026-03-09 02:09 UTC an automated maintenance window started in eu-west (route reload + instance drain) per maintenance-notice eu-west-2026-03-09
3) Traffic for 8 minutes was routed to fallback pools while maintenance progressed; customer expected pinned requests to remain on their reserved pool, not be routed to hosted fallback,
4) Customer observed higher-than-expected per-token rates in billing reports and an automated invoice auto-pay failure on 2026-03-10.
logs: 2026-03-09T02:11:05Z router: req_id=abc123 org=brightnote key=xxxx route=hosted-fallback reason=pool_unavailable pin_header=redwood/open-7b-v2-pin-2026-02-15
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: routing policy incorrectly ignored model pin flag during the maintenance-induced pool transition, allowing fallback to hosted pools that apply hosted tariff metering tags.
Checked routing logs (datadog stream: dd://logs/router?from=2026-03-09T02:00&to=2026-03-09T03:00) — multiple entries show 'reason=pool_unavailable' and 'route=hosted-fallback' for pinned requests.

Billing pipeline shows metering tag 'billing_tier=hosted' attached to affected postbacks (postback ids start with pb-77xx). Metering pipeline does not apply additional correction when 'pin' header is present.

Dedicated control-plane shows reserved pool (ded-eu-021) had scaled-down active instances during the drain; autoscaler policy temporarily marked instances as unhealthy which triggered routing failover.
Reproduction attempt on staging: simulated drain with same autoscaler signal; observed routed pinned traffic to fallback unless 'force-pin-during-drain' flag is set in routing config.

Root cause candidate: a safety-first routing rollback introduced in rollout ROL-2026-02-27 disabled honoring 'X-Model-Pin' during pool_unavailable events to protect against stale pins; this had unintended billing side-effect.
Estimated affected volume for BrightNote: ~42k tokens billed at hosted rate between 02:10-02:18 UTC (approx. $9.84 in overage).
comments: 2026-03-10 08:32 - Support (Maya Chen): Logged ticket on behalf of BrightNote. Customer provided a snippet of their billing line items and the API request headers. Requested provisional credit and engineering investigation.
2026-03-10 11:45 - SRE (Jules Kline): Confirmed maintenance window for eu-west and observed router failover events. Escalated to routing team. Linking incident channel #inc-routing-euw.

2026-03-10 15:02 - Routing Eng (Omar Patel): Found rollout ROL-2026-02-27 introduces 'strict-failover' mode. Opening PR to change behavior to preserve pin header when reserved pool exists but is draining. PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/5621
2026-03-11 09:18 - Billing (Asha Mehta): Identified postbacks pb-7789..pb-7798 associated with hosted-tier tags. Preparing provisional credit calculation for customer.
resolution: Provisional credit applied for identified hosted-billed tokens; routing team merged change to preserve model pin during graceful drain. Billing applied a $12.00 credit to BrightNote's account to cover the measured overage and a buffer. Ongoing action: run backfill audit to ensure no remaining impacted postbacks; billing to confirm on next invoice.
